subject: Day 13: growth spurt likely tomorrow; line up the EPDS
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 13. End of week two. Most term infants have regained birth weight. The first growth spurt typically opens tomorrow with a sharp rise in feeding frequency that resets within two days.

Action items
- Plan the next two days lightly — the spurt window is not the time for commitments that cannot move.
- Schedule the EPDS maternal mood screen for this coming week; if the pediatrician will not run it, Anoushka can take it herself and a score above 10 warrants a call to her OB.
- Open the 529 plan if the SSN is in hand. 529 plan overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
- Apply for paternity leave if not already on it; coordinate employer leave with any state paid-family-leave benefit.
- Keep the feeding log current ahead of the 1-month visit.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump fully detached or nearly so; baby acne visible; cluster feeding may begin tonight.
- [low concern] Sustained eye contact appearing during feeds.
- [monitor] Mother's mood at the two-week mark — baby blues easing is expected; persistence is the signal to act.
- [call within 24h] Projectile vomiting after most feeds. Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Keep daily tummy time near 15 minutes, split across short bouts after feeds. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take conversational turns with his coos — respond, pause, respond again. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Read aloud for ten minutes with exaggerated, rhythmic prosody.
- Give him a slow side-to-side moving target to track during an alert window.

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first growth spurt underway.
- Day 14-21: EPDS maternal mood screen.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
